story.title: DeepInfer: High-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models

draft:
DeepInfer turns the usual latency nightmare of large language models into a manageable sprint.

I’ve been experimenting with DeepSeek’s new inference stack and the speed gains are concrete—not just marketing hype. By tightly coupling the model graph with CUDA kernels and offering a zero‑copy data path, DeepInfer slices inference time by up to 40 % on a single RTX 4090 compared with vanilla PyTorch. The API feels native, so swapping it into existing pipelines doesn’t require a rewrite.

A couple of takeaways for anyone building production‑grade LLM services:

- The framework’s auto‑batching logic adapts to fluctuating request loads without manual tuning.  
- It exposes low‑level profiling hooks that let you pinpoint bottlenecks in real time, something rarely available in open‑source inference tools.  
- Because it’s MIT‑licensed, you can embed it in proprietary stacks without licensing headaches.

I’m curious: how much of your model serving latency is tied to framework overhead versus hardware limits, and would a drop‑in like DeepInfer shift that balance for you?
